sources.entry: Kutt - Modern URL shortener with support for custom domains and custom URLs. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: Kutt is a self-hostable URL shortener built on Node.js with support for custom domains, custom short URLs, link statistics, and an admin panel.
summary.what_it_does: Kutt creates short links that can be served from custom domains, with options to set a custom URL, password, description, and expiration time for each link. Users can view, edit, delete and manage their links and see private statistics for shortened URLs. An admin page manages users and links. It exposes a RESTful API and supports OpenID Connect (OIDC) login. Setup uses Node.js 20+ with SQLite by default, and it can optionally use Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB, and Redis for caching. Registration, anonymous links, and the login form can be disabled through environment variables, and the look can be changed with custom CSS, images, and templates.
use_cases: shorten links on my own custom domain
track click statistics for short links
share short links with a team using managed user accounts
integrate link shortening into scripts via the REST API
use as default shortener in ShareX
how_to_run: npm run dev (development) or npm start (production)
notable: Zero-configuration default with SQLite and no build step
Custom domain support with per-link custom URLs
Themes and template overrides via a /custom folder
Multiple docker-compose variants for SQLite, Postgres, and MariaDB with Redis
Ecosystem of third-party clients in C#, Python, Ruby, Rust, Go, Node.js, and more
caveats: The kutt.it domain is not owned by the project and may be a phishing site; use kutt.to
Custom domains need SSL certificates generated manually, per the README
JWT_SECRET is required in production; some optional features (email, OIDC) need extra configuration
keywords: shorten links on my own domain
